lines.japanese: 二時間目が終わったあとの休み時間。化学実験室をあとにした私は、かすかな焦りを感じていた。
lines.english: During the break after second period, I leave the chemistry lab starting to feel a little anxious.

lines.japanese: 胃のあたりに微妙な違和感があるのだ。
lines.english: Something feels slightly off around my stomach.

lines.japanese: 早い話が空腹である。
lines.english: In short, I'm hungry.

lines.japanese: そろそろ平時であれば「今日のごはん何にしよっかな～あ」と思いめぐらす頃合だ。しかし今日の私にはそれが出来ない。何故ならお金がないから。
lines.english: This is about when I'd normally start wondering, ‘What should I have for lunch today?’ But today I can't. Because I have no money.

lines.japanese: ちょっと待て。いまからこんなじゃ、私はきょう一日を生きぬくことなんて出来ないのではあるまいか。
lines.english: Hang on. If I'm already like this, can I possibly survive the whole day?

lines.japanese: よし、こんなときこそ想像力だ。肉でも魚でもケーキでも、夢の中でたらふく食べよう。
lines.english: Right. This is exactly when I need my imagination. Meat, fish, cake—I'll feast on whatever I like in my dreams.

lines.japanese: いや、しかし、それほど真に迫ったイメージを編みだすには相応のエネルギーが必要じゃあるまいか。
lines.english: But wouldn't conjuring up an image that convincing take a fair amount of energy?

lines.japanese: うん、腹が減っては戦もできないってことで、まず先に肉や魚やケーキを食べよう。なん（略）
lines.english: Yes. An army marches on its stomach, so first let's eat some meat, fish, and cake. Just k—(etc.)

lines.japanese: 教室に戻るや、すぐさま自分のかばんを確認した。
lines.english: As soon as I get back to the classroom, I check my bag.

lines.japanese: 財布を忘れたのは確かだが、私はいつも、それとは別に小銭入れを常備している。場合によっては五百円硬貨の一枚や二枚、眠っているかもしれない。それだけあれば学校食堂においては充分だ──
lines.english: I definitely forgot my wallet, but I always carry a separate coin purse. There might be a five-hundred-yen coin or two sleeping in there. That would be plenty for the school cafeteria—

lines.japanese: ──と勇んで中身を机に広げる。
lines.english: —so, full of hope, I spill its contents onto my desk.

lines.japanese: じゃらららっ。
lines.english: Clatter, clatter.

lines.japanese: ひい、ふう、みい……。
lines.english: One, two, three...
183 yen.

lines.japanese: 現実を受けいれたくなくて、しばらく凝視していた。あるいは来たる飢饉に備え、少しでもカロリー消費を抑えるための生存本能が働いたのかもしれない。
lines.english: I stare at it for a while, unwilling to accept reality. Or maybe my survival instinct has kicked in, conserving every possible calorie in preparation for the coming famine.

lines.japanese: ふと頭上から、ぶっきらぼうな男の声が降ってきた。
lines.english: Suddenly, a curt male voice drops down from above.

lines.japanese: 「知ってる」
lines.english: “I know.”

lines.japanese: 私は一度頷いてから顔を上げた。
lines.english: I nod once, then look up.

lines.japanese: 針生先輩がいた。
lines.english: Hariu is there.

lines.japanese: てか、いるなよ。
lines.english: Actually, don't be there.

lines.japanese: 「てか、いるなよ」
lines.english: “Actually, don't be there.”

lines.japanese: 頭に湧いた不満をそのまま口に出した。このひととはいいかげん付き合いが長いので、お互い思ったことは思ったまま言ってしまう仲だった。
lines.english: I say exactly what I was thinking. I've known him long enough that we can both say whatever comes into our heads.

lines.japanese: もっとも針生先輩の方は、相手が初対面だろうとシャレが通じまいと言葉を選ばない、無敵の自由びとなんだけども。
lines.english: Though Hariu never bothers choosing his words, even with someone he's just met or who can't take a joke. An unstoppable free spirit.

lines.japanese: 「先輩、よく下級生の教室フツーに入ってこられるね」
lines.english: “You've got some nerve just walking into a lower grade's classroom like it's nothing.”

lines.japanese: 私は空きっ腹を押さえながら言った。
lines.english: I say this with a hand on my empty stomach.

lines.japanese: 「あ？　なんか問題あった？」
lines.english: “Huh? That a problem?”

lines.japanese: 「若干」
lines.english: “A little.”

lines.japanese: みんな見てるし。
lines.english: Everyone's watching, for one thing.

lines.japanese: ただでさえ針生先輩は学園内でそこそこ有名人。良い意味でも悪い意味でも。
lines.english: Hariu is already fairly famous around school. For good reasons and bad.

lines.japanese: まずは良い意味から紹介しよう。学力は全国でもトップレベル。一年で辞めてるけど陸上部でいっぱい賞とってた。
lines.english: Let's start with the good. Academically, he's among the best in the country. He won a bunch of awards on the track team, though he quit after a year.

lines.japanese: 黙ってればヴィジュアルはいいから憧れてる女子も少なくない。あとクイズ番組に出て優勝してた。
lines.english: He's good-looking when he keeps his mouth shut, so quite a few girls admire him. Also, he appeared on a TV quiz show and won.

lines.japanese: ちなみにこれはオフレコだから学校のみんなは知らないけど、ロックバードっていうインディーズのバンドでドラム叩いてる。
lines.english: Incidentally, this is off the record, so nobody at school knows, but he plays drums in an indie band called Rockbird.

lines.japanese: メジャーシーンから注目されてるぐらいには好評らしい。私の趣味じゃなかったけども。
lines.english: Apparently, they're doing well enough to get noticed in the mainstream music scene. Not to my taste, though.

lines.japanese: で、悪い方。こっちは枚挙にいとまがない。とりあえず職員室のブラックリスト筆頭。授業はサボるわ、校則は破るわ、屁理屈で教師へこますわ、まあヒドイもの。
lines.english: And now the bad. Too much to list. For a start, he's at the top of the teachers' blacklist. Skips class, breaks rules, argues the teachers into the ground with ridiculous logic. It's pretty awful.

lines.japanese: 生徒間での受けも最悪。うちの学校はガチガチの進学校で目立った不良グループみたいのってないんだけど、いちおう成績下位者が集められるＨ組っていうのがあって──
lines.english: He's just as unpopular with the other students. This is a strictly academic school, so we don't have any obvious gang of delinquents, but there's a class H where they gather the low scorers—

lines.japanese: ──一度そこの恐めなおにいさんたちから、針生先輩にいわゆる呼び出しが掛かったらしい。結果はひとりで十数人を返り討ち。付いた仇名がインテリヤクザ。以来、誰も彼に近づかなくなった。やれやれだね。
lines.english: —and apparently, the scary guys there once summoned Hariu for a little talk. Result: he took on more than a dozen of them alone and beat them. They nicknamed him the Intellectual Gangster. Nobody's gone near him since. Honestly.

lines.japanese: 「つくづく不思議なんだけど、先輩なんで退学にならないの？」
lines.english: “I keep wondering. Why haven't you been expelled?”

lines.japanese: 「あァ、そりゃあ、その辺は計算してるからなァ」
lines.english: “Oh, I've got that all calculated.”

lines.japanese: 針生先輩はふらふら上下左右を見回しながら言った。
lines.english: Hariu says this while idly looking up, down, and all around.

lines.japanese: 「出席日数とか？」
lines.english: “Like your attendance?”

lines.japanese: 「それ以外にも色々だよ。たとえば俺は今年、行くつもりもない大学をいくつも受験することになってる」
lines.english: “All sorts of other things too. For instance, this year I'm taking entrance exams for a bunch of colleges I have no intention of attending.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ。なんで？」
lines.english: “Huh. Why?”

lines.japanese: 「ンー、大人の約束だから、詳しいことは言えないなァ。まあヒントは……この学校のパンフレットに、合格率って載ってたろ。アレは進学率じゃなくて合格率ってところがミソだな」
lines.english: “Mm, it's an arrangement among adults, so I can't tell you the details. Here's a hint, though... The school brochure listed its college acceptance rate, right? The trick is that it's the acceptance rate, not the enrollment rate.”

lines.japanese: 独り言のように呟きながら、眼鏡の奥の黒い瞳を忙しなく走らせている。
lines.english: Muttering as though he's talking to himself, he keeps his dark eyes darting behind his glasses.

lines.japanese: 「ふうん」
lines.english: “Hmm.”

lines.japanese: 私は口を開かぬまま無感動な音を漏らした。学園のせこいイメージアップ大作戦なんて、迫りくる空腹感に比べればわりとどうでもいい。
lines.english: I make the indifferent noise without opening my mouth. The school's petty image-boosting schemes don't matter much compared with the hunger closing in on me.

lines.japanese: 「なんてゆか、うちの学校も教え子には清廉潔白だ清貧貞潔だ言っといて、意外としたたかなんだねえ」
lines.english: “I don't know. Our school tells its students to be honest, incorruptible, content with poverty, and chaste, but it's surprisingly calculating itself.”

lines.japanese: 「そりゃあなァ、ヒトひとり捕ったって色んな顔があンだ。ヒトの集合体だったら尚更だろ」
lines.english: “Of course. Even one person has all sorts of faces. All the more so when you get a whole bunch of people together.”

lines.japanese: 今度は机の上の硬貨を、一枚一枚手に取って観察しはじめた針生蔵人。
lines.english: Now Kuroudo Hariu starts picking up the coins on my desk one by one to examine them.

lines.japanese: 彼は玉泉とは別の意味で、相手の目を見て話せないひとなのだ。好奇心と探求心にとり憑かれている彼は、一分一秒をも惜しんで、いつでもこの世のあらゆる情報を取りこんでいないと気が済まないらしい。
lines.english: He's another person who can't look you in the eye when he talks, but for a different reason than Tamaizumi. Possessed by curiosity and the urge to investigate, he apparently can't bear to waste a second. He has to keep taking in every kind of information the world offers.

lines.japanese: ここまで来ると、もはや強迫観念だよね。天才となんとかは紙一重、なんて昔のひとはよくぞ言ったものだ。おかげで私たちに集まっていた数多の視線が、蜘蛛の子を散らしたように逃げさってゆくよ。
lines.english: At this point, it's practically an obsession. Whoever first said there's a fine line between genius and you-know-what really knew what they were talking about. Thanks to him, all those eyes on us have suddenly found other places to look.

lines.japanese: 「あァ、そういや、明日香のツレってどいつ？」
lines.english: “Oh, yeah. Which one's your guy, Asuka?”
“...Sorry?”

lines.japanese: 「おまえの今カレだよ。このクラスじゃない？」
lines.english: “Your current boyfriend. Isn't he in this class?”

lines.japanese: 先輩はさっさとコインを捨てて、ふたたび教室中にきょときょと目を走らせていた。
lines.english: He quickly abandons the coins and starts darting his eyes around the classroom again.

lines.japanese: なにを……なにを言いだすんだ突然……びび、びっくりするじゃないか。
lines.english: What... what are you saying all of a sudden...? Y-you startled me.

lines.japanese: 「いや、あの、えっ？　なに、そんなこと聞きにきたの先輩？」
lines.english: “No, um, huh? What, did you come here to ask that?”

lines.japanese: 「やァ、違うけど、もののついでだ。形だけでもおまえが恋人役として選んだ男なら、普通なはずはないもんなァ。今度はどんな馬鹿だい」
lines.english: “Nah, just while I'm here. Even if it's only for show, a guy you picked to play your boyfriend can't be normal. What kind of idiot is it this time?”

lines.japanese: 「馬鹿じゃないよ」
lines.english: “He's not an idiot.”

lines.japanese: ふんだ。いきなりの話題転換に驚いちゃったけども、平静を取りもどしてにやり。
lines.english: Hmph. The sudden change of subject surprised me, but I regain my composure and grin.

lines.japanese: 「これ以上は教えないけどね」
lines.english: “But I'm not telling you anything else.”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　なんで」
lines.english: “Huh? Why not?”

lines.japanese: 「なんでって……」
lines.english: “Why not...”

lines.japanese: なんでだ？
lines.english: Why not?

lines.japanese: べつに、針生先輩は口堅いし、ていうか話すような友達もいないだろうし、教えちゃっても問題はないような……？
lines.english: Hariu can keep a secret. Or rather, he probably doesn't have any friends to tell. So there shouldn't be a problem with telling him... should there?

lines.japanese: でも、んー、なんとなくこう、抵抗あるなあ。
lines.english: But, hmm. Somehow, I'm reluctant.

lines.japanese: 「うん、教えない。なんかヤだ。なんか恥ずかしい」
lines.english: “No, I'm not telling. I just don't want to. It's embarrassing.”

lines.japanese: 「恥ずかしい……？」
lines.english: “Embarrassing...?”

lines.japanese: 退屈しのぎを探してさまよい続けていた瞳が、不意に止まった。焦点は私。
lines.english: The eyes that have been wandering in search of something to relieve his boredom suddenly stop. On me.

lines.japanese: な、なんだ、やるのかこのやろう。私は子供のころ好きだった特撮ヒーローの構えを真似た。じゅわっ。
lines.english: Wh-what? You wanna fight, you bastard? I imitate the stance of the live-action superhero I liked as a kid. Hyah!

lines.japanese: 「おまえ……」
く、来るなら来い。じゅわっ。
lines.english: C-come on, then. Hyah!

lines.japanese: 「……はン、なるほどな。今回は本気で惚れてンのか」
lines.english: “...Hah. I see. You've actually fallen for him this time.”

lines.japanese: 「はああ？」
lines.english: “Whaaat?”

lines.japanese: 私は「じゅわっ」の態勢のまま固まった。
lines.english: I freeze in my ‘Hyah!’ pose.

lines.japanese: 「だれが？　だれを？」
lines.english: “Who? For whom?”

lines.japanese: 「明日香がその男を。あァ、まだ自覚なかったか」
lines.english: “You, for that guy. Oh, you hadn't realized yet?”

lines.japanese: 「ありえない」
lines.english: “Impossible.”

lines.japanese: 「そうかァ？　でもそう考えれば説明つくンだけどなァ色々、おまえの顔がいま赤い理由とかも？」
lines.english: “Really? It'd explain a lot, though. Like why your face is red right now?”

lines.japanese: 「う、嘘をゆうなっ。じょわっち」
lines.english: “D-don't lie! Hyaaah!”

lines.japanese: 「はン。まあいいよ、どのみちおまえに教える気がないなら、俺も詮索するほど暇じゃねえし。そんなことよりアレだ、辞書貸してくれ辞書、英和辞書」
lines.english: “Hah. Whatever. If you don't want to tell me, I don't have the time to pry anyway. More importantly, lend me a dictionary. A dictionary. English-Japanese.”

lines.japanese: 言うだけ言って言い逃げか。
lines.english: So he says his piece, then runs away from it.

lines.japanese: まあね。いいけどね。でもこうなったらタダじゃ貸さないけどね。
lines.english: Well, fine. That's okay. But now he's not getting it for free.

lines.japanese: 私は机の脇の置きっぱ用バッグから、先輩ご所望の辞典を取りだして掲げた。
lines.english: I take the dictionary he wants out of the bag I leave beside my desk and hold it up.

lines.japanese: 「先輩にしちゃあ珍しいねえ。たまには授業、真面目に受けるんだ？」
lines.english: “That's unusual for you. Actually taking a class seriously for once?”

lines.japanese: 「逆だ、逆。まともに受けてちゃ時間の浪費だから、辞書でも読んで暇つぶすんだよ」
lines.english: “The opposite. The opposite. Paying attention would be a waste of time, so I'm gonna read the dictionary to pass it.”

lines.japanese: 「ン。じゃ借りてくぞ」
lines.english: “Right. I'll borrow that.”

lines.japanese: 「おっと待ったぁ」
lines.english: “Whoa, hold it.”

lines.japanese: 先輩が私の釣り餌に手を伸ばしたところで、すかさず後ろへ退避。
lines.english: As soon as he reaches for my bait, I move it behind me.

lines.japanese: 「食糧と交換ってどうすか？」
lines.english: “How about trading me some food for it?”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: レーザーのような鋭い視線が、辞書→私の顔→机の上の小銭→私の顔とすばやく射抜いていった。
lines.english: His laser-sharp gaze shoots from the dictionary to my face, down to the coins on my desk, then back to my face.

lines.japanese: 「ふン」
lines.english: “Hmph.”

lines.japanese: 「笑うなよ」
lines.english: “Don't laugh.”

lines.japanese: 「サプリでいいか？」
lines.english: “Supplements okay?”

lines.japanese: 「ふざけないでください」
lines.english: “Please don’t mess with me.”

lines.japanese: 「俺の昼メシはこれなんだよ」
lines.english: “That's my lunch.”

lines.japanese: 「私は学食のチキンソテー定食が食べたい」
lines.english: “I want the cafeteria's sautéed chicken meal.”

lines.japanese: 「腹に入れば大差ねえよ」
lines.english: “Not much difference once it's in your stomach.”

lines.japanese: 「いまの私はビタミンやミネラルより満腹感を得たいのだが」
lines.english: “Right now I'd rather have a full stomach than vitamins and minerals.”

lines.japanese: 「中枢神経に作用するのもある。食欲消えるぞ」
lines.english: “Some of them work on the central nervous system. They’ll kill your appetite.”

lines.japanese: 「分かった、前言撤回。５００円貸してください」
lines.english: “Okay, forget what I said. Please lend me five hundred yen.”

lines.japanese: 「金おろしてなくてなァ、いま手持ちないんだよ」
lines.english: “Haven't taken out any cash. Don't have any on me.”

lines.japanese: 「まじか。ちょっと跳んでみろ」
lines.english: “Seriously? Jump a little. Let me hear.”

lines.japanese: 「ファック」
lines.english: “Fuck.”

lines.japanese: 先輩は品のない悪態をつきながらもその場で二度三度と垂直跳びをした。変なところで律儀なひとだ。しかし耳をそばだてても、残念ながら小銭の跳ねる音は聴かれなかった。
lines.english: Despite that vulgar curse, he jumps straight up two or three times. He's oddly obliging about some things. But however closely I listen, there's sadly no jingle of coins.

lines.japanese: そして四度目のジャンプでとつぜん風のように私の横を吹きぬけ──
lines.english: On his fourth jump, he suddenly blows past me like the wind—
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: ──右手に持っていた辞書をあざやかにかすめ取っていった。
lines.english: —and neatly snatches the dictionary from my right hand.

lines.japanese: 「どーも。借りてくよ」
lines.english: “Thanks. I'll borrow it.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、どろぼー！」
lines.english: “Hey, thief!”

lines.japanese: 「いや、代金そこ置いた」
lines.english: “Nah, I left your payment there.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 先輩の顎が示す先を目で追った。１８３円分の硬貨に混じって、いつの間にかアーモンド形のタブレットが１錠転がっていた。
lines.english: I follow the direction of his chin. Somehow, an almond-shaped tablet has appeared among my 183 yen in coins.

lines.japanese: 「ちょっ、だからサプリは……！」
lines.english: “Hey, I told you, supplements aren't...!”

lines.japanese: しかし視点を戻したとき、すでに針生蔵人は消えていた。
lines.english: But by the time I look back, Kuroudo Hariu is already gone.

lines.japanese: 手品師かあのひとは。
lines.english: Is the man a magician?

lines.japanese: あとに残された私は、クラスメイトたちの好奇の目に晒されていた。
lines.english: Left behind, I find myself exposed to my classmates' curious eyes.

lines.japanese: 羽田君も見ていた気がするけど、案の定、私がそちらの方を向いたときにはもう、彼はまぶたを伏せて教室を出ていってしまった。
lines.english: I think Haneda was watching too, but sure enough, by the time I turn his way, he's already lowered his eyes and left the classroom.

lines.japanese: 食に固執する浅ましい女と思われたかもしれない。やってくれたなハリュー・クロード。
lines.english: Maybe he thinks I'm a greedy girl obsessed with food. You've really done it now, Claude Haryuu.

lines.japanese: 私は逆恨みして先輩の置き土産をぼりぼりかじった。
lines.english: Unfairly resenting him, I crunch down on the parting gift he left me.

lines.japanese: きょうのランチは苦虫を噛みつぶしたような味がした。
lines.english: Today's lunch tastes as bitter as my expression.

lines.japanese: 「ぷはっ……はあ、はあ、はあ……」
lines.english: “Pwah... Hah, hah, hah...”

lines.japanese: カルキ臭満点の水道水で、口の中の砕片を残らず流しこんだ。
lines.english: I wash down every last fragment with tap water reeking of chlorine.

lines.japanese: 「あ゛ー、苦かった……」
lines.english: “Ughhh, that was bitter...”

lines.japanese: ていうか、過去形じゃなくてまだ苦い。ナウ苦い。依然として苦い。いや、苦いのかコレ？
lines.english: Actually, forget the past tense. It's still bitter. Bitter right now. Continually bitter. Or is this even bitterness?

lines.japanese: もうね、この後味はね、謎サプリの苦味と水道水の臭味とが織りなす地獄のケミカルハーモニーだね。
lines.english: This aftertaste, you know, is a chemical harmony from hell, woven out of the mystery supplement's bitterness and the tap water's foul flavor.

lines.japanese: 制服姿がまばらに散った休み時間の廊下に、さっき教室から出ていった彼を見た。羽田君だ。
lines.english: In the hallway, sparsely dotted with uniforms during the break, I see the boy who left the classroom earlier. Haneda.

lines.japanese: ほう、彼にしては珍しい、同級生と話しているではないか。しかも女子だ。
lines.english: Oh, that's unusual for him. He's talking to a classmate. A girl, at that.

lines.japanese: 女子？
lines.english: A girl?

lines.japanese: 誰だろう。私はハンカチで口を拭いながら、目を凝らして近付いてゆく。
lines.english: Who is it? Wiping my mouth with my handkerchief, I peer closer as I approach.

lines.japanese: やましな？
lines.english: Yamashina?

lines.japanese: あれ？　でも、きょう山科って休みだったはず──
lines.english: Huh? But I thought Yamashina was absent today—

lines.japanese: ──そっか、じゃあ遅刻していま来たのか。また病院かな。大変だよね。
lines.english: —oh, so she was late and just got here. The hospital again, maybe. Must be hard.

lines.japanese: あの子と初めて会ったのは、去年の四月の入学式。出席番号順に並ばされた列の中、ワ行の私はいちばん後ろ。そしてそのひとつ前が山科京だった。
lines.english: I first met her at the entrance ceremony in April last year. We were lined up by attendance number, which put me, a Watarai, at the very end. Immediately ahead of me was Miyako Yamashina.

lines.japanese: 園長やら教頭やら学年主任やらの長話がつづくあいだ、私と山科とその前のＤ子（ごめんＤ子、名前忘れた。お元気ですか？）は、三人でひそひそ話に興じて退屈な時間をつぶした。
lines.english: While the school director, vice principal, grade head, and so on gave their long speeches, Yamashina, I, and the girl ahead of her, D (sorry, D, I've forgotten your name. How are you?), passed the time whispering together.

lines.japanese: 新入生当時はみな新しい学校の新しい教室でお互い知った顔もなく、そのままなんとなく三人で授業の確認をしたり、昼食を取ったり、教室移動したりして──
lines.english: Back then, we were all new students in new classrooms at a new school, with no familiar faces. The three of us just sort of started checking our class schedules together, eating lunch together, moving between classrooms together—

lines.japanese: ──そのうちになんとなく他の二人組や三人組と合流したり、なんとなく誰かが別のグループへ移ったりしていって、一学期が終わるころにはなんとなく私と山科は別グループに所属していた。ちなみにＤ子も。
lines.english: —then sort of joined up with other pairs or trios, and someone would sort of move into a different group. By the end of the first term, Yamashina and I had sort of ended up in separate groups. D too, incidentally.

lines.japanese: いま振りかえってみるに、つくづく縁は異なものだなあと思う。
lines.english: Looking back now, I really do think human connections are strange things.

lines.japanese: 私にしては珍しいことだが、実は山科京とはけっこう波長が合ってたのである。趣味や性格は微妙に合わなかったけども、なんというか、お互いイイカンジの間合いを把握していたというか──
lines.english: Unusual for me, but Miyako Yamashina and I were actually on pretty similar wavelengths. Our tastes and personalities didn't quite match, but somehow, we both understood a comfortable distance—

lines.japanese: ──双方とも基本的には単独行動が好きで、でもたまに気まぐれで「どっか寄ってく？」なんて声かけたりもする、そんな付かず離れずの距離感が心地よかった。気がする。
lines.english: —we both basically liked doing things alone, but would occasionally ask, on a whim, ‘Wanna stop somewhere?’ That not-too-close, not-too-distant feeling was comfortable. I think.

lines.japanese: 大して実のある話はした覚えがないけど、私と彼女ふたりだけのときの会話はこんなだった。
lines.english: I don't remember talking about anything very substantial, but when it was just the two of us, our conversations went like this.

lines.japanese: 「山科ー」
lines.english: “Yamashina.”
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: 「最近どう？」
lines.english: “How've you been lately?”

lines.japanese: 「んー……サックスブルー、かなあ」
lines.english: “Mm... Saxe blue, maybe.”

lines.japanese: 「あはっ、押しつけがましい素朴？」
lines.english: “Ha! Simplicity that tries too hard?”

lines.japanese: 「そんな感じ。不安にさせるメルヘン色」
lines.english: “Something like that. An unsettling fairy-tale color.”

lines.japanese: 「くふふ、あるある」
lines.english: “Hee hee, I know the feeling.”

lines.japanese: （数分間の沈黙）
lines.english: (Several minutes of silence.)

lines.japanese: 「渡来さん、最近どう？」
lines.english: “How've you been lately, Watarai?”

lines.japanese: 「あー？　あー、そうねー……ほうじ茶、とか」
lines.english: “Huh? Oh, let's see... Roasted green tea, or something.”

lines.japanese: 「んん？　クリアな郷愁？」
lines.english: “Hmm? Clear nostalgia?”

lines.japanese: 「惜しい。冬眠する記憶」
lines.english: “Close. Hibernating memories.”

lines.japanese: 「くすっ、なにそれ、引っかけじゃん……」
lines.english: “Heh. What's that? A trick question...”

lines.japanese: あの頃は、あんな意味不明な連想ゲームの、いったい何が面白かったんだか。
lines.english: What on earth did we find fun about those incomprehensible association games back then?

lines.japanese: 実際すぐに飽きた。
lines.english: We did get bored of them pretty quickly.

lines.japanese: でもあの頃あの瞬間、私たちは「くだらねー」「それはねー」「意味わかんねー」とか言いながらも、地球中でただ二人にしか分からない秘密の世界観をたしかに共有していたんだ。
lines.english: But back then, in those moments, even while saying ‘That's stupid,’ ‘No way,’ or ‘What does that even mean,’ we really shared a secret view of the world that only two people on the whole planet understood.

lines.japanese: 短かったけどね。
lines.english: Briefly, though.

lines.japanese: もしも人類が、私と山科ふたりだけだったとしたら、たぶんいい親友になってたと思う。そんな想像。
lines.english: If Yamashina and I had been the only two humans, I think we probably would've become best friends. That's my little imagining.

lines.japanese: だけど私はみんなの誘いを断りきれずに、一方あの子はみんなの誘いを断りすぎて、そうして気が付いたら私たちは同じ教室の遠いところにいた。うそ。三コ隣り。そんな遠くない。物理的にはね。
lines.english: But I couldn't refuse people's invitations, while she refused too many of them. Before we knew it, we were far apart in the same classroom. Not really. Three seats apart. Not that far. Physically, anyway.

lines.japanese: その山科が。へえ、ふうん、そう。羽田君と、へえ、仲よかったんだ。ふうん。
lines.english: And that Yamashina. Huh. Hmm. I see. So she and Haneda... huh. They're close. Hmm.

lines.japanese: いいけどね、べつにどうだって。
lines.english: Fine, though. Doesn't matter to me.

lines.japanese: でも何の話をしてるんだろう。気になるね。なんてね。ならないけどね。
lines.english: But what are they talking about? I'm curious. Just kidding. I'm not, though.

lines.japanese: おいおい楽しそうだな。羽田、きさま私には人間嫌いと言っておきながら。
lines.english: Hey, hey. You look like you're having fun. Haneda, you bastard. You told me you hated people.

lines.japanese: いいけどね、べつに。
lines.english: It's fine, though. Whatever.

lines.japanese: 行こ行こ。
lines.english: Let's go, let's go.

lines.japanese: 不運は重なるものらしい。
lines.english: Apparently, bad luck comes in bunches.

lines.japanese: ふだん私は数人のお昼メイツと連れだって学食へ行く。
lines.english: Normally, I go to the cafeteria with a few lunch buddies.

lines.japanese: むやみに貸しを作りたくはなかったが、背に腹は代えられないので、今日は彼女らのうちの誰かに昼食代を借りるつもりだった。
lines.english: I don't like owing people favors for no good reason, but I don't have a choice. Today, I was planning to borrow lunch money from one of them.

lines.japanese: しかし四時間目の現代文が終わったあと、私はレポートの提出が遅かったことを理由に、担当教員からちょいとした雑用を言いつかってしまった。
lines.english: But after fourth-period modern Japanese, the teacher assigned me a little errand because I'd handed in my report late.

lines.japanese: 用事を片付けて教室に戻ってくると、皆はもういなかった。私たちのコミュニティには、相手を待たない思いやりという不文律があったのだ。
lines.english: By the time I finish it and get back to the classroom, everyone's gone. Our little community has an unwritten rule: kindness means not waiting for each other.

lines.japanese: まあね。いつもの私ならね。待たれることを逆にありがた迷惑と感じたかもだけどね。
lines.english: Well, yes. On an ordinary day, I'd probably find being waited for more of a burden than a favor.

lines.japanese: 私は小銭入れを掴んでひとり学食へ向かった。
lines.english: I grab my coin purse and head to the cafeteria alone.

lines.japanese: よく考えたらそう悲観することもない。１８３円あればパンの一個ぐらい買える。乙女の胃袋にはそれで充分だ。たぶん。
lines.english: Thinking about it, there's no need to be so pessimistic. 183 yen will buy at least one bread roll. That's plenty for a girl's stomach. Probably.
“Gah.”

lines.japanese: 少年漫画みたいな声を漏らしてしまうほど、パン売り場には長蛇の列が出来ていた。
lines.english: The line at the bread counter is long enough to make me blurt out a noise straight from a boys' comic.

lines.japanese: これレジへ辿りつくまでに昼休み終わっちゃわない？　という危惧を抱きつつも、とりあえず最後尾に並んだ。
lines.english: Won't lunch break be over by the time I reach the register? Worried as I am, I join the end of the line for now.

lines.japanese: そして、しばらくして気付いた。
lines.english: After a while, I notice.

lines.japanese: 「あ、彼氏」
lines.english: “Oh, my boyfriend.”

lines.japanese: あいだに五人挟んだ微妙な距離に、羽田君の物憂げな背中があった。
lines.english: With five people between us—an awkward distance—there's Haneda's melancholy back.

lines.japanese: 声をかけるには遠い。いちおうクラスメイトとして、手ぐらいは振っておきたいところだけど、いや、全ー然こっち見てないね。
lines.english: Too far away to call to him. I'd at least like to wave as a classmate, but no, he's not looking this way at all.

lines.japanese: ま、そうか。私だって、いま自分の五つ後ろに誰がいるかなんて考えもしない。
lines.english: Well, of course. I'm not thinking about who's five places behind me either.

lines.japanese: はあ。列の進み悪いなあ。
lines.english: Sigh. This line is moving so slowly.

lines.japanese: ふうん。羽田君、パン食かあ。
lines.english: Hmm. So Haneda's having bread.

lines.japanese: あはは、そういえば一年のころ、彼よくパンの買い出し係させられてたなあ──
lines.english: Ha ha, come to think of it, in our first year he was always being made to go buy bread for people—

lines.japanese: ──なんて、さっきの山科メモリーズの余韻もあってか、私はふたたび去年の春へ思いを馳せた。
lines.english: —and maybe because those memories of Yamashina are still lingering, I find myself thinking back to last spring again.

lines.japanese: 記憶の想起はメンタルトレーニングの一環。こういう空き時間を有効利用するにも適してるね。
lines.english: Recalling memories is a form of mental training. A good way to make use of idle time like this.

lines.japanese: 「おお、明日香じゃん」
lines.english: “Oh, hey, Asuka.”

lines.japanese: 耳障りな声が鼓膜を撫でた。
lines.english: An unpleasant voice strokes my eardrums.

lines.japanese: 寒気のようなものを感じて私は声の主を睨んだ。あ、いや、睨んじゃいかん。
lines.english: Feeling something like a chill, I glare at its owner. Oh, no. Mustn't glare.

lines.japanese: 「なになに、おまえ何してんの。何してんのじゃねーか。パン買うんだよなそりゃ、ぎゃはは」
lines.english: “What's up, what's up? What're you doing? Wait, that's stupid. Buying bread, obviously. Gahaha!”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「エじゃねーよ、俺ボケたんだから笑えって、へへ」
lines.english: “Don't ‘huh’ me. I made a joke. You're supposed to laugh. Heh heh.”

lines.japanese: いえ、違います。いまの「え？」は「あんた誰？」の「え？」であり、暗に「どこでお会いしたか存じませんが私はあなたに下の名前で呼び捨てされるような謂われはございません」の意味を含んでおります。
lines.english: No, that's not it. That ‘huh?’ meant ‘Who are you?’ It implicitly included, ‘I have no idea where we met, but you have no grounds whatsoever to address me so familiarly by my first name.’

lines.japanese: 「オマエ何、最近バイトか何かしてんの？　メールの返事ぜんぜんよこさねーじゃん、どんだけ忙しンだよ」
lines.english: “What, you got a part-time job lately or something? You never reply to my messages. How busy can you be?”

lines.japanese: 「あー」
ああ、はいはい。先月、文化祭のクジ引き屋で受付係やってた、馴れ馴れしさに定評のあるナントカ先輩ですね。はいはい、なるほど、あのしばしば送られてくる謎の駄メールはあなたでしたか。
lines.english: Oh, right, right. You're Mr. Something-or-Other, the guy manning the raffle booth at last month's school festival, famed for getting too familiar. Right, I see. Those strange, pointless emails that keep turning up are yours.

lines.japanese: てか私、あなたにアドレス教えてないんですけど。私が欲しかったのは２８インチ大型テレビの当選通知であって、名前も知らない上級生からの怪文書ではないんですけど。
lines.english: Except I didn't give you my email address. What I wanted was a notification that I'd won the big twenty-eight-inch TV, not bizarre messages from some older student whose name I don't even know.

lines.japanese: てか貴様、個人情報をなんだと思ってる。訴えるぞ。
lines.english: Hey, you bastard. What gives you the right to use my personal information? I'll sue you.

lines.japanese: ていうことをぴしゃりと言ってやるべきか、でもこういう手合いに逆恨みされると厄介なんだよなあ、などと逡巡しているうちにもナントカ先輩はひとりで勝手に喋る喋る喋る。
lines.english: Should I tell him off like that? But this sort of guy is a pain if he starts holding a grudge. While I hesitate, Mr. Something-or-Other just keeps talking, talking, talking.

lines.japanese: そのトークの寒々しさたるや、これはこれで一周まわって面白いぞの境地に達してるんだけども、いかんせん無駄に声が大きくて、列の前後の皆さんが不快な思いをされておるのではと不安になる。
lines.english: His conversation is so painfully unfunny it's almost come full circle and become funny again. Unfortunately, he's pointlessly loud, and I worry that the people ahead of and behind us in line are having an unpleasant time.

lines.japanese: 「つかオマエ、疲れてんの？　すっげタルそーじゃん、ダイジョブかよ」
lines.english: “Hey, are you tired or something? You look seriously out of it. You okay?”

lines.japanese: ちょっとちょっと、手が気安いって。触るな下衆。
lines.english: Hey, hey. Your hand's a little too familiar. Don't touch me, creep.

lines.japanese: 私は「はあ」という露骨に不快な声とともに肩を引いて、偽善者の接触から逃れた。
lines.english: With an openly displeased sigh, I draw my shoulder back, escaping the hypocrite's touch.

lines.japanese: あ、羽田君いま一瞬こっち見た。うわあ、痛い友達がいると思われちゃったなあ。
lines.english: Oh, Haneda just looked this way for a second. Great. He must think I have an embarrassing friend now.

lines.japanese: はあ、逃げるか……ここまで並んでもったいないけど……。
lines.english: Sigh. Maybe I should run... Shame after standing in line this long...

lines.japanese: てゆか、パンが買えないのは残念だけど……。
lines.english: And it's a shame not to get any bread...

lines.japanese: 「あっ！」
lines.english: “Oh!”

lines.japanese: 「な、なに？　え、どうしたの？」
lines.english: “Wh-what? Huh? What's wrong?”

lines.japanese: 「すみません、邪魔っ」
lines.english: “Sorry, you're in the way!”

lines.japanese: 私はナントカ先輩を押しのけてパンの列を飛びだした。
lines.english: I push Mr. Something-or-Other aside and leap out of the bread line.

lines.japanese: 希望の星が通りすぎていったからだ。
lines.english: Because a star of hope has just passed by.

lines.japanese: 「やましなー！　ぜに貸してー！」
lines.english: “Yamashina! Lend me some cash!”

lines.japanese: 私が発見したとき山科京は、脇目も振らず前のめりの姿勢でずんずん歩いていた。
lines.english: When I spot Miyako Yamashina, she's striding straight ahead without looking aside, leaning forward.

lines.japanese: 朝の通勤電車から降りたお父さんみたいな、男前の速度。握りこぶしの親指が唇に押しつけられていた。
lines.english: A manly pace, like a dad who's just stepped off his morning commuter train. The thumb of her clenched fist is pressed against her lips.

lines.japanese: あーれれ、なんか不機嫌そうな歩き方……うーん、たまにああなんだよなあ、あの子。
lines.english: Uh-oh. That walk looks kind of grouchy... Hmm. She gets like that sometimes.

lines.japanese: キホンおとなし系で、若干フシギ入りなんだけど、ときどきあんな感じ。妙にギラついてるというか、なんかテンパってたりするの。気分屋ちゃんなんだね。
lines.english: She's basically quiet, with a touch of oddness, but sometimes she's like this. Strangely intense, or kind of worked up. A moody girl.

lines.japanese: だから今、私が呼びかけたときなんかも威勢よく体ごと振りかえって──
lines.english: So when I call out to her now, she swings her whole body around energetically—

lines.japanese: 「お金っ！？」
lines.english: “Money?!”

lines.japanese: ──ほら、予想通り声が元気だよ。今日はそういう日みたい。
lines.english: —see? Her voice is lively, just as I expected. Apparently, today's one of those days.

lines.japanese: 「うん……え、ダメ？」
lines.english: “Yeah... Huh, is that a no?”

lines.japanese: 私は努めてフラットな声で会話を繋いだ。こういうときの山科に合わせるのはツライので、悪いけどマイペース。
lines.english: I deliberately keep my voice level as I carry on the conversation. Matching Yamashina's mood when she's like this is hard, so, sorry, I'll stick to my own pace.

lines.japanese: 「なになにどしたのなんでっ？」
lines.english: “What, what happened, why?”

lines.japanese: 水鉄砲みたいな言葉。目を剥くような強めの笑顔になった。
lines.english: Words like a squirt gun. She breaks into an intense, wide-eyed smile.

lines.japanese: 白い歯が覗くほどにニカッと笑っているけれどそれは、はにかむように息を漏らす普段の静かな笑い方じゃない。
lines.english: She's grinning broadly enough to show her white teeth. Not her usual quiet, shy little laugh, almost just an escaping breath.

lines.japanese: 「んんっ」
lines.english: “Ahem.”

lines.japanese: そして今度は俯いて咳払いを一回。そのまま大きく肩を上下させた。呼吸が荒い。どっか走ってきたのかね、君は。
lines.english: Then she looks down and clears her throat once. Her shoulders rise and fall heavily. She's breathing hard. Were you running somewhere or what?

lines.japanese: 「なに山科、きょうテンション高いデー？」
lines.english: “What is it, Yamashina? Having a high-energy day?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ？　うーん、普通かな」
lines.english: “Huh? Hmm... Just a normal day, I guess.”

lines.japanese: 顔を上げて、繕うように笑った。まだ少し、息の乱れの余韻があった。
lines.english: She looks up and puts on a smile. Her breathing is still a little uneven.

lines.japanese: 普通、ねえ……まあ、本人がそう言うならいいけども。
lines.english: Normal, huh... Well, if she says so.

lines.japanese: 「あーいいや、聞いて。あのね、いま私、財布を忘れて深刻な大飢饉なの」
lines.english: “Oh, never mind. Listen. I forgot my wallet, and right now I'm facing a very serious famine.”

lines.japanese: 私はお腹に手を置きつつ、しかし声だけは真面目風で訴えた。
lines.english: I plead my case with a hand on my stomach, though only my voice is serious.

lines.japanese: 山科は「うんうん」という感じで頷いていたけど、気付いたらずーいぶん長いこと全身をうんうん揺らしていた。
lines.english: Yamashina nods in a ‘Yes, yes’ sort of way, but before I know it, she's been bobbing her entire body for quite a while.

lines.japanese: 「あした返すから、悪い、５００円貸して」
lines.english: “I'll pay you back tomorrow. Sorry, but lend me five hundred yen.”

lines.japanese: そう言うと彼女はにっこり笑った。
lines.english: At that, she smiles.

lines.japanese: 「いいよ。ちょっと待って」
lines.english: “Sure. Wait a second.”

lines.japanese: 「ぃよし！」
lines.english: “Yesss!”

lines.japanese: 山科が小銭入れを開けた。私は小さくガッツポーズ。いい子だね山科。ありがとうね山科。
lines.english: Yamashina opens her coin purse. I make a small fist pump. You're a good girl, Yamashina. Thank you, Yamashina.

lines.japanese: しかし。
lines.english: However.

lines.japanese: 「あ、残金２１０円」
lines.english: “Oh. I've got 210 yen left.”

lines.japanese: 「うそ」
lines.english: “No way.”

lines.japanese: ぬかよろこび……？
lines.english: I got my hopes up for nothing...?

lines.japanese: 厨房から漂ってくるカレーの匂いが、嫌味ったらしく鼻腔を通っていった。
lines.english: The smell of curry drifting from the kitchen passes spitefully through my nostrils.

lines.japanese: 「ごめん……ええ？　あれ？　なんで」
lines.english: “Sorry... Huh? Wait. Why?”

lines.japanese: 愕然とする私を気に病んでか、彼女はスカートのポケットへ何度も手を出し入れしだした。
lines.english: Maybe worried about my stunned expression, she starts putting her hands into her skirt pockets and taking them out again, over and over.

lines.japanese: 「ごめん……ごめんね、渡来さん……」
lines.english: “Sorry... I'm sorry, Watarai...”

lines.japanese: 「い、いいよいいよ、気にしないで。べつに私、そこまでお腹すいてたわけでもないんだぁ」
lines.english: “I-it's fine, it's fine. Don't worry. It's not like I was that hungry.”

lines.japanese: きゅうぅぅぅ、ぴるるるるぅ～……
lines.english: Grrrrrrr, trrrrrrrrr...

lines.japanese: 冗談みたいなタイミングで鳴る私の内臓は、なかなかお笑いの才能があるよね。
lines.english: My internal organs, sounding off with such comically perfect timing, have quite a talent for comedy.

lines.japanese: 「ううん、おかしいの、あるんだよたぶん。だって５００円だよ？　あるでしょ。あるでしょ５００円ぐらい、ぜったいあるって」
lines.english: “No, it's strange. I probably have it. I mean, it's five hundred yen, right? I'd have that. I'd have five hundred yen, wouldn't I? I definitely have it.”

lines.japanese: いや、いいの。お願い、あきらめて。そんな小さいポケット、何度もまさぐる必要ないでしょ。
lines.english: No, it's okay. Please give up. You don't need to keep rummaging in those tiny pockets.

lines.japanese: 「貸さなきゃ、ほんと貸さなきゃ。お金ぐらい貸せるもん、そのぐらい出来るもん。待ってね、ちょっと待ってね、いま手の感覚なくてアレだけど、すぐ見つけるからちょっと待ってね」
lines.english: “I have to lend it to you. I really do. I can lend money. I can do at least that much. Wait, just wait a second. I can't feel my hands right now, but I'll find it in a moment, so just wait.”

lines.japanese: 「いいよ。そんな、一所懸命あさったって……山科？　山科？」
lines.english: “It's okay. Searching that hard isn't... Yamashina? Yamashina?”

lines.japanese: あららら、ムキになってる。私は彼女の腕に手を置いた。
lines.english: Oh dear. She's getting worked up. I put a hand on her arm.
“Huh?!”

lines.japanese: 全身びくっと揺れる。小動物ですか。
lines.english: Her whole body jolts. Are you a small animal?
“Wh-what...?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、なにって」
lines.english: “Well, what do you mean, ‘what’?”

lines.japanese: こっちが聞きたい。なにそれ、いまの濃い芸風。でも言いたいことは伝わったさ、同志。
lines.english: That's my question. What's with that over-the-top performance? But I understand what you're trying to say, comrade.

lines.japanese: 「私が悪かったよ。ごめん、金欠なのはよく分かったから、そんな必死にアピールしなくても」
lines.english: “My fault. Sorry. I get that you're broke, so you don't have to try so desperately to show it.”

lines.japanese: 「あ……うん、うんうん」
lines.english: “Oh... Yeah, yeah, yeah.”

lines.japanese: 山科は小刻みに何度も頷いた。うんうんうんうん。
lines.english: Yamashina nods over and over in little jerks. Yes, yes, yes, yes.

lines.japanese: 「こっちこそごめんね、力になれなくて」
lines.english: “I'm sorry too. For not being any help.”

lines.japanese: 恥じいるように目を伏せる彼女は、そうだ、これが私の知ってる山科京だ。
lines.english: She lowers her eyes as though ashamed. Yes. This is the Miyako Yamashina I know.

lines.japanese: 「てか、どしたの山科、いま熱っぽいとか？」
lines.english: “Hey, what's up, Yamashina? Are you feeling feverish or something?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？　あ、うん、そうなの。ちょっと変でしょ、ぼーっとしてた？」
lines.english: “Huh? Oh, yeah, that's it. I was a little strange, wasn't I? All out of it?”

lines.japanese: 「や……ぼーっていうか、むしろ、がーって感じ？」
lines.english: “No... More ‘vrrrooom’ than ‘duhhh,’ I’d say?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ？　ひどーい」
lines.english: “Huh? That's mean.”

lines.japanese: いや、的確な表現だったと思うんだけど。がーって感じ。
lines.english: No, I think it was an accurate description. ‘Vrrrooom.’

lines.japanese: 私たちはぽつぽつ語りながら、昼休み終わり際の廊下をのんびり歩いた。
lines.english: We stroll through the hallway near the end of lunch break, talking now and then.

lines.japanese: ぽつぽつってのは、本当にぽつぽつだ。
lines.english: And now and then really means now and then.

lines.japanese: 私が窓の外の空を「広っ！」とか当たり前のこと思いながらぼけーっと眺めていても、彼女は好きな男子の話とか好きな俳優の話とか好きなスポーツ選手の話とかで遮ったりしてこない。
lines.english: Even when I stare blankly at the sky outside the window, thinking something obvious like ‘So big!’, she doesn't interrupt me with talk about boys she likes, actors she likes, or athletes she likes.

lines.japanese: 色気がないと言われたら、まあ、それはそうなんだけども──
lines.english: If you said we lacked romance, well, yes, that's true—

lines.japanese: 「そんなことよりお腹すいたよね」
lines.english: “More importantly, I'm hungry, you know?”

lines.japanese: 「そうなんだ」
lines.english: “Oh, you are?”

lines.japanese: ──そんなような会話をぽつぽつとしたわけさ。
lines.english: —and that's the sort of conversation we have, now and then.
